docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Welcome to the documentation for the Cross-Dataset Discovery Service.

This service lets users search across DataGEMS datasets with natural language. It provides an API to:

  • Search the indexed content of all datasets a user has access to, using keyword (BM25), semantic, or hybrid search, optionally assisted by an LLM.
  • Ingest datasets into the search index from their dataset profiles, and remove them again.

docs.title: How to Use This Documentation
docs.text:
• System: Learn about the high-level Architecture, the Security model, and the Datastores.
  • API: Find detailed information on the API endpoints, the status and error codes, and the OpenAPI specification.
  • Setup & Monitoring: Get instructions on Deployment, Configuration, Logging, and Maintenance, and see the Automations that build, scan, test and publish the service.
  • Developer Guides: Extend the retrieval framework with the Onboarding guide, and see how the service is checked in Quality Assurance.

docs.title: API Overview
docs.text: The Cross-Dataset Discovery service exposes a RESTful API for searching the indexed datasets and for managing which datasets are indexed.

docs.title: Base URL
docs.text:
Base URL: https://datagems-dev.scayle.es/cross-dataset-discovery/

The running service also serves its own interactive documentation at /swagger and /redoc, and the raw specification at /openapi.json. The full specification is also available on the OpenAPI Specification page.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text: All endpoints except GET / and GET /health require a valid JWT Bearer token in the Authorization header. The token must carry the user or dg_user role, or a privileged role (dg_admin, dg_system, dg_dataset-curator). Each endpoint additionally checks dataset-level grants, as listed below. See Security for details.

docs.title: Endpoints at a Glance
docs.text:
Method Path Purpose Dataset grant required POST /search/ Search the index dg_ds-browse (results are filtered) POST /search-ap/ Search, using an analytical pattern as request and response dg_ds-browse (results are filtered) POST /corpus-analysis-search/ LLM-assisted search for text passages dg_ds-browse (results are filtered) POST /ingest/ Index a dataset from its profile (background job) dg_ds-edit GET /ingest/ List ingestion jobs dg_ds-edit on the dataset_id filter (privileged roles can list all) GET /ingest/{job_id} Get the status of an ingestion job dg_ds-edit DELETE /dataset/{dataset_id} Remove a dataset from the index dg_ds-delete GET / Liveness check none (no authentication) GET /health Readiness check of the service and its dependencies none (no authentication)

Callers with a privileged role bypass all dataset grant checks.

docs.title: Search
docs.text:
Performs a search query against the indexed datasets.

  • Endpoint: POST /search/
  • Description: Submits a natural language query and returns a ranked list of relevant results. Supports Sparse (BM25), Dense (Semantic), and Hybrid search modes.
  • Request Body:
{
  "query": "string",
  "k": 5,
  "dataset_ids": [
    "string"
  ],
  "search_mode": "sparse"
}
  • query: Required. The natural language query.
  • k: Optional. Number of results to return, between 1 and 100 (default 5).
  • dataset_ids: Optional. Restricts the search to these datasets. The list is intersected with the datasets the user may browse; if nothing remains, an empty result list is returned. Must not be an empty list.

  • search_mode: Optional. Can be "sparse" (default), "dense", or "hybrid".

  • Response Body (Success):

{
  "query_time": 42.17,
  "results": [
    {
      "content": "The main text content of the search result.",
      "dataset_id": "uuid-of-the-source-dataset",
      "object_id": "uuid-of-the-source-object",
      "similarity": 12.3
    }
  ]
}
  • query_time: Processing time in milliseconds.
  • object_id: The file object the result comes from. For dataset-level results (such as the dataset description), this is the same as dataset_id.
  • similarity: BM25 score, cosine similarity, or RRF score, depending on search_mode.

Results from datasets the user is not authorized to browse are always removed, whether or not dataset_ids was given.

docs.title: Search via Analytical Pattern
docs.text:
• Endpoint: POST /search-ap/
  • Description: The same search as POST /search/, but the request and response are DataGEMS analytical patterns (APs).
  • Request Body: An analytical pattern that contains a node labelled CDD_Operator. The search arguments are read from that node's properties. query is required; k, dataset_ids, and search_mode are optional and mean the same as in POST /search/.
{
  "ap": {
    "nodes": [
      {
        "id": "op-1",
        "labels": ["CDD_Operator"],
        "properties": {
          "query": "string",
          "k": 5,
          "search_mode": "hybrid"
        }
      }
    ],
    "edges": []
  }
}
  • Response Body (Success): The same analytical pattern, updated with the results:
    • Any nodes previously connected as outputs of the CDD_Operator node are removed.
    • One sc:Dataset node is added per result dataset, and one cr:FileObject node per result object.
    • Each cr:FileObject node gets an output edge from the CDD_Operator node and a distribution edge from its dataset.
    • The full search response (query_time, results) is merged into the pattern's top-level metadata.
{
  "ap": {
    "nodes": [
      { "id": "op-1", "labels": ["CDD_Operator"], "properties": { "query": "string" } },
      { "id": "dataset-uuid", "labels": ["sc:Dataset"] },
      { "id": "object-uuid", "labels": ["cr:FileObject"] }
    ],
    "edges": [
      { "from": "op-1", "labels": ["output"], "to": "object-uuid" },
      { "from": "dataset-uuid", "labels": ["distribution"], "to": "object-uuid" }
    ]
  },
  "metadata": {
    "query_time": 42.17,
    "results": [ ... ]
  }
}

A pattern without a CDD_Operator node, without a query, or with invalid optional arguments results in a 500 Internal Server Error.

docs.title: Corpus Analysis Search
docs.text:
• Endpoint: POST /corpus-analysis-search/

  • Description: An LLM-assisted search for text passages that answer a natural language question. The steps are:

    1. An LLM extracts the text request from the question. It also extracts time-period, location, and language constraints, but these are not applied yet.
    2. The index is searched with the extracted request.
    3. The LLM scores each result for relevance and drops results that score below 3. Fewer than k results may therefore be returned.

    Each LLM step tries the configured LLM providers in order (see Configuration). If a step still fails, the service uses the original question and the unscored results instead of failing the request. Dataset access filtering works the same as in POST /search/. * Request Body:

{
  "query": "string",
  "dataset_ids": [
    "string"
  ]
}
  • query: Required. The natural language question.
  • dataset_ids: Optional. Same meaning as in POST /search/.
  • k (deprecated): Number of results to retrieve before LLM scoring (default 50, maximum 100).
  • search_mode (deprecated): Retrieval strategy (default "dense").

k and search_mode are still accepted, but will be removed once the API chooses them automatically.

  • Response Body (Success): The same shape as POST /search/, plus each result's indexed metadata:
{
  "query_time": 1830.5,
  "results": [
    {
      "content": "The main text content of the search result.",
      "dataset_id": "uuid-of-the-source-dataset",
      "object_id": "uuid-of-the-source-object",
      "similarity": 0.71,
      "metadata": {
        "dataset_id": "uuid-of-the-source-dataset",
        "file_object_id": "uuid-of-the-source-object",
        "original_filename": "/s3/path/to/file.json"
      }
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: Ingest a Dataset
docs.text:
• Endpoint: POST /ingest/?path_to_profile={path}&replace={true|false}

  • Description: Indexes a dataset described by a dataset profile (JSON). The service reads the profile from path_to_profile, a path on the service's mounted storage (for example /s3/...). The caller needs a dg_ds-edit grant on the profile's @id, or a privileged role.

    Ingestion can take a long time, so it runs as a background job. The endpoint returns immediately with a job_id to poll with GET /ingest/{job_id}. * Query Parameters: * path_to_profile: Required. Path to the dataset profile JSON, as seen by the service. * replace: Optional (default false). If the dataset is already indexed: * false: nothing is done and the request returns 200 with status skipped. * true: the dataset's existing indexed content is deleted and rebuilt from the profile. * Response Body (202 Accepted, job scheduled):

{
  "job_id": "uuid-of-the-job",
  "status": "pending",
  "dataset_id": "uuid-of-the-dataset"
}
  • Response Body (200 OK, already indexed and replace=false):
{
  "job_id": null,
  "status": "skipped",
  "dataset_id": "uuid-of-the-dataset"
}

docs.title: Dataset Profile
docs.text:
The profile must contain the dataset @id and description, plus the list of files to index:

{
  "@id": "uuid-of-the-dataset",
  "name": "Dataset name",
  "description": "Dataset description (indexed as its own search item).",
  "files": [
    {
      "file_object_id": "uuid-of-the-file",
      "source_file": "/s3/path/to/file.csv",
      "original_format": "csv"
    }
  ]
}

If the profile cannot be read or has no @id, the request fails immediately with 400. If description is missing, the job fails.

Each file is handled according to its original_format:

original_format How it is indexed Extra file fields used csv, xlsx, xls One item per row, serialized as column: value text (numeric values are left out) – sql-db One item per table row (serialized as above), read from the database named name on one of the configured SQL servers. Tables larger than SQL_DB_MAX_TABLE_MB (default 512 MB) instead get one item per column, built from a sample of rows (see Configuration) name (database), tables[].name (optional; defaults to all tables) text, application/pdf One item per pre-computed chunk chunked_content (a list of sections, each with a chunks list) json, application/json Records split into token-based chunks; the title is prepended to each chunk content_fields (default ["text"]), metadata_fields (default: all other fields), title_field (default "title") docx, pptx, ipynb Text split into token-based chunks –

Files with any other format are skipped (logged as a warning).

docs.title: Get Ingestion Job Status
docs.text:
• Endpoint: GET /ingest/{job_id}
  • Description: Returns the state of an ingestion job. Requires the same dg_ds-edit grant (or privileged role) as starting the job.
  • Response Body (Success):
{
  "job_id": "uuid-of-the-job",
  "status": "completed",
  "dataset_id": "uuid-of-the-dataset",
  "profile_path": "/s3/path/to/profile.json",
  "replace": false,
  "requested_by": "sub-claim-of-the-caller",
  "items_submitted": 12345,
  "items_indexed": 12345,
  "points_in_qdrant": 12345,
  "deleted_count": null,
  "error": null,
  "started_at": "2026-10-14T09:00:00.000000Z",
  "finished_at": "2026-10-14T09:12:31.000000Z"
}

stateDiagram-v2
    direction LR
    [*] --> pending: POST /ingest/
    pending --> running: job starts
    running --> completed: success
    running --> failed: error
    pending --> interrupted: service restart
    running --> interrupted: service restart
    note right of failed: Fix the cause, then re-ingest with replace=true
    note right of interrupted: Re-ingest with replace=true

Ingestion job statuses.

  • status: one of:
    • pending: scheduled, not started yet.
    • running: in progress.
    • completed: finished successfully.
    • failed: stopped with an error (see error).
    • interrupted: the service restarted before the job finished. The dataset may be partially indexed; run the ingestion again with replace=true.
  • requested_by: The sub claim of the caller that started the job.
  • items_submitted: Number of items sent for embedding. Set when the job completes.
  • items_indexed: Number of points this job wrote to Qdrant. Set when the job completes; normally equal to items_submitted.
  • points_in_qdrant: Total number of the dataset's points in Qdrant after the job. After a fresh or replace=true ingestion it should equal items_indexed. A mismatch means points were lost, or another job wrote to the same dataset at the same time.
  • deleted_count: Number of previously indexed points removed (set only when replace=true).
  • error: The failure reason (set only when the job fails or is interrupted).

Job records are stored in Qdrant (in their own collection), so they survive service restarts.

docs.title: List Ingestion Jobs
docs.text:
• Endpoint: GET /ingest/?status={status}&dataset_id={dataset_id}&limit={n}
  • Description: Lists ingestion jobs, newest first. Callers with a privileged role can list all jobs. Other callers must pass dataset_id and hold a dg_ds-edit grant on that dataset; otherwise the request is rejected with 403.
  • Query Parameters:
    • status: Optional. Only return jobs with this status (pending, running, completed, failed, or interrupted).
    • dataset_id: Optional for privileged callers, required for everyone else. Only return jobs for this dataset.
    • limit: Optional. Maximum number of jobs to return (default 10).
  • Response Body (Success): The job records, in the same format as GET /ingest/{job_id}:
{
  "jobs": [
    {
      "job_id": "uuid-of-the-job",
      "status": "interrupted",
      "dataset_id": "uuid-of-the-dataset",
      ...
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: Delete a Dataset
docs.text:
• Endpoint: DELETE /dataset/{dataset_id}
  • Description: Removes all of a dataset's indexed content. The source data is not touched. The caller needs a dg_ds-delete grant on the dataset, or a privileged role.
  • Response Body (Success):
{
  "dataset_id": "uuid-of-the-dataset",
  "deleted_count": 12345
}

If the dataset is not in the index, the endpoint returns 404.

docs.title: Liveness
docs.text:
• Endpoint: GET /
  • Description: Returns a static response without checking dependencies. Used as the Kubernetes liveness probe. No authentication required.
  • Response Body (Success):
{
  "status": "ok",
  "message": "Cross Dataset Discovery API is running."
}

docs.title: Health Check
docs.text:
Verifies the operational status of the API and its dependencies.

  • Endpoint: GET /health
  • Description: Checks that the search component is initialized and that Qdrant and the TEI embedding service are reachable. Used as the Kubernetes readiness probe. No authentication required. If a check fails, it returns 424 Failed Dependency naming the failing component.
  • Response Body (Success):
{
  "status": "ok",
  "message": "All dependencies are healthy."
}

See Status & Error Codes for the error responses of all endpoints.

docs.title: System Architecture
docs.text: The Cross-Dataset Discovery Service is part of the DataGEMS ecosystem. It indexes the content of DataGEMS datasets and lets users search across them with natural language. It orchestrates an embedding service, a vector database and, for one endpoint, an LLM.

docs.title: Core Components
docs.text:
flowchart TB
    client["Client<br/>(user or DataGEMS service)"]
    api["Cross-Dataset Discovery API<br/>FastAPI · BM25 via FastEmbed"]

    subgraph sec["Security"]
        oidc["OIDC provider<br/>(Keycloak)"]
        gw["DataGEMS Gateway"]
    end

    subgraph search["Search infrastructure"]
        tei["TEI<br/>BAAI/bge-m3 embeddings"]
        qdrant[("Qdrant<br/>index + ingestion jobs")]
    end

    llm["LLM providers<br/>SCAYLE, Bedrock fallback"]

    subgraph src["Dataset sources (read-only)"]
        storage[("Dataset storage<br/>profiles and files")]
        sql[("Dataset database servers<br/>(PostgreSQL)")]
    end

    client -->|"REST + JWT"| api
    api -->|"token validation"| oidc
    api -->|"dataset grants"| gw
    api -->|"dense embeddings"| tei
    api -->|"search, upload, delete"| qdrant
    api -.->|"LLM-assisted steps"| llm
    api -.->|"ingestion"| storage
    api -.->|"ingestion"| sql

The API and the services it uses, grouped by role. TEI is deployed together with the API; the other services are shared or external. Dotted lines are used only by some endpoints.

  1. FastAPI Application (API Pod): The entry point of the service. It authenticates and authorizes requests, runs searches, and runs dataset ingestion as background jobs. It computes sparse (BM25) vectors locally with FastEmbed (CPU).

  2. Vector Database (Qdrant): Stores the dense and sparse vectors of every indexed item, together with its text and metadata. It performs the actual retrieval: nearest-neighbour search for dense vectors, an inverted index for sparse vectors, and Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF) for hybrid search. It also stores the ingestion job records. See Datastores.

  3. Embedding Service (TEI Pod): A Hugging Face Text Embeddings Inference service. It produces dense vectors (BAAI/bge-m3, 1024 dimensions) for queries and for ingested content.

  4. Security Layer: Validates OIDC tokens and queries the DataGEMS Gateway for the caller's dataset grants. See Security.

  5. LLM: Used only by POST /corpus-analysis-search/, to extract the text request from a question and to score results for relevance. By default the model is served by SCAYLE (OpenAI-compatible API), with Amazon Bedrock as a fallback if a SCAYLE call fails. See Configuration.

  6. Dataset sources (read-only): During ingestion the API reads dataset profiles and files from mounted dataset storage, and sql-db datasets from the DataGEMS database servers.

docs.title: Search Flow
docs.text:
A POST /search/ request goes through these steps:

sequenceDiagram
    participant C as Client
    participant A as API
    participant O as OIDC provider
    participant G as DataGEMS Gateway
    participant T as TEI
    participant Q as Qdrant

    C->>A: POST /search/ (JWT, query, search_mode)
    opt First request of the process
        A->>O: Fetch public keys (then cached)
    end
    A->>A: Validate JWT and roles
    opt Caller has no privileged role
        A->>G: Query dg_ds-browse grants
        G-->>A: Authorized dataset IDs
    end
    opt sparse or hybrid
        A->>A: Compute BM25 sparse vector
    end
    opt dense or hybrid
        A->>T: Embed query
        T-->>A: Dense vector
    end
    A->>Q: Query with vector(s) and dataset_id filter
    Q-->>A: Top-k points (RRF in hybrid mode)
    A->>A: Drop results from unauthorized datasets
    A-->>C: 200 results + query_time

A POST /search/ request.

  1. Auth: The Security Layer validates the JWT and checks the caller's roles. Unless the caller has a privileged role, it fetches the IDs of the datasets the caller may browse from the DataGEMS Gateway.
  2. Filter: If the request has dataset_ids, they are intersected with the authorized datasets and passed to Qdrant as a dataset_id filter.
  3. Vector Generation:
    • Sparse mode: The API computes a BM25 sparse vector locally.
    • Dense mode: The API sends the query text to TEI to get a dense vector.
    • Hybrid mode: Both are computed.
  4. Retrieval: The API queries Qdrant:
    • Sparse: Searches the sparse vectors. Qdrant applies IDF weighting.
    • Dense: Searches the binary-quantized dense vectors, fetching twice as many candidates as needed and rescoring them with the full vectors.
    • Hybrid: Runs both searches, then merges them with RRF.
  5. Response: Results from datasets the caller is not authorized for are removed, and the rest are returned with their scores.

POST /search-ap/ runs the same flow, reading its arguments from an analytical pattern and writing the results back into it.

POST /corpus-analysis-search/ adds two LLM steps around the retrieval:

  • Before step 3, the LLM rewrites the question into a text request, which is what gets searched.
  • After step 4, the LLM scores each result and drops those below the threshold.

Each LLM call tries the configured providers in order. If all of them fail, the original question and the unscored results are used.

docs.title: Ingestion Flow
docs.text:
A POST /ingest/ request goes through these steps:

sequenceDiagram
    participant C as Client
    participant A as API
    participant J as Background job
    participant DS as Dataset sources
    participant T as TEI
    participant Q as Qdrant

    C->>A: POST /ingest/?path_to_profile=...
    A->>DS: Read profile
    A->>A: Check dg_ds-edit grant (via Gateway)
    A->>Q: Is the dataset already indexed?
    alt Indexed and replace=false
        A-->>C: 200 status: skipped
    else Not indexed, or replace=true
        A->>Q: Save job record (pending)
        A-->>C: 202 job_id
        A-)J: Start background job
        par Background job
            J->>Q: Job record: running
            opt replace=true
                J->>Q: Delete the dataset's points
            end
            loop Stream items in batches
                J->>DS: Read files / SQL tables
                J->>T: Embed batch (dense)
                J->>J: Compute BM25 sparse vectors
                J->>Q: Upload points
            end
            J->>Q: Rebuild vector index, apply quantization
            J->>Q: Job record: completed or failed
        and Client polls
            loop Until completed or failed
                C->>A: GET /ingest/{job_id}
                A->>Q: Read job record
                A-->>C: Job status
            end
        end
    end

A POST /ingest/ request and the background job it starts.

  1. Read profile: The API reads the dataset profile from the dataset storage. The caller must hold a dg_ds-edit grant on the profile's dataset (or a privileged role).
  2. Check existing data: If the dataset already has points in Qdrant and replace is false, the request returns skipped.
  3. Create job: A job record (pending) is saved in Qdrant, the background job is scheduled, and the API returns 202 with the job_id.
  4. Background job:
    1. If replace is true, the dataset's existing points are deleted.
    2. Items are produced, one at a time, from:
      • the dataset description;
      • each file in the profile, using the loader for its format (tables row by row, documents in token-based chunks, pre-chunked text and PDFs as given, SQL tables from the database servers).
    3. Items are processed in batches: the dense vectors come from TEI and the sparse vectors are computed locally. The resulting points are uploaded to Qdrant. Items are streamed, so large datasets are never fully loaded into memory.
    4. After the upload, Qdrant's vector indexing and quantization are applied to the collection.
    5. The job record is updated as it progresses, and finally set to completed (with item counts) or failed (with the error).

The client polls GET /ingest/{job_id} for progress. If the service restarts while a job is running, the job is marked interrupted at the next start.

DELETE /dataset/{dataset_id} removes all points with that dataset_id from Qdrant.

docs.title: Automations
docs.text:
This project uses GitHub Actions to automate builds, code analysis, security scanning, testing, and documentation deployment. Apart from image publishing, which runs on every version tag, all workflows are started manually from the repository's Actions tab (workflow_dispatch).

Workflow Repository Trigger Purpose Build and Push Search API Docker Image code Push of a v* tag Build and publish the Docker image Vulnerability Scan (On-Demand) code Manual Trivy scan of the repository configuration and a published image CodeQL Scan (On-Demand) code Manual Static code analysis Code Metrics (On-Demand) code Manual Radon complexity and maintainability report Test Scenario (On-Demand) code Manual API tests against the deployed service Deploy Docs (On-Demand) docs Manual Publish this documentation site Deploy to Dev (On-Demand) deployment (dev) Manual Apply the Kubernetes manifests to the development cluster (see Deployment) Deploy to Prod (On-Demand) deployment (prod) Manual Apply the Kubernetes manifests to the production cluster (see Deployment)

docs.title: Dockerfile
docs.text:
The production container image is built by the Dockerfile in the root of the code repository, in two stages:

  • Stage 1 (Builder): Installs CPU-only PyTorch and the API's Python dependencies, and pre-downloads the models the service needs at runtime: the FastEmbed Qdrant/bm25 model and the BAAI/bge-m3 tokenizer.
  • Stage 2 (Final): Copies only the installed packages, the model cache and the application code onto a clean python:3.12-slim base. It creates a non-root appuser, defines a HEALTHCHECK, and starts the gunicorn server.

See Deployment for details.

docs.title: Docker Image Publishing
docs.text:
Workflow: .github/workflows/docker-publish.yml

This workflow builds the service's Docker image and publishes it to the GitHub Container Registry (ghcr.io).

  • Trigger: Runs automatically whenever a Git tag matching v* (e.g. v1.17.2) is pushed.
  • Process:
    1. Logs into the GitHub Container Registry using the workflow's GITHUB_TOKEN.
    2. Uses docker/metadata-action to derive the image tag from the Git tag. The image gets exactly that tag; no latest tag is published.
    3. Builds the image with Docker Buildx, reusing layers from the GitHub Actions cache to speed up builds.
    4. Pushes the image to ghcr.io/datagems-eosc/cross-dataset-discovery-api.

docs.title: Vulnerability Scanning
docs.text:
Workflow: .github/workflows/vulnerability-scan-on-demand.yml

This workflow scans the project's configuration and a published Docker image using the Trivy security scanner.

  • Trigger: Manual. It requires an image_tag input naming the published image to scan.
  • Process:
    1. Configuration Scan: Scans the Dockerfile and other configuration files of the default branch for security misconfigurations.
    2. Image Scan: Pulls ghcr.io/datagems-eosc/cross-dataset-discovery-api:<image_tag> and scans its operating system packages and Python libraries for known vulnerabilities (CVEs) of CRITICAL or HIGH severity.
    3. Artifacts: The JSON reports of both scans are uploaded as build artifacts (vulnerability-config-scan and vulnerability-image-scan).

docs.title: Static Code Analysis
docs.text:
Workflow: .github/workflows/code-scan-on-demand.yml

This workflow runs GitHub CodeQL to find potential bugs, security vulnerabilities, and quality issues.

  • Trigger: Manual.
  • Process:
    1. Runs two analysis jobs: one for the Python code and one for the GitHub Actions workflow files.
    2. Uses the security-extended and security-and-quality query suites.
    3. Uploads the results to the repository's Security tab, under Code scanning alerts.

docs.title: Code Metrics
docs.text:
Workflow: .github/workflows/code-metrics-on-demand.yml

This workflow reports on the complexity and maintainability of the API code using Radon.

  • Trigger: Manual.
  • Process:
    1. Installs the radon Python package.
    2. Analyzes the cross_dataset_discovery/darelabdb/api_datagems_cross_dataset_discovery/app directory:
      • Maintainability Index (MI): A score from 0 to 100 indicating how easy the code is to maintain.
      • Cyclomatic Complexity (CC): The number of independent paths through each function, indicating its complexity.
      • Raw Lines of Code (LOC): Basic code size metrics.
    3. Uploads the report as a build artifact named code-metrics-report.

docs.title: API Tests
docs.text:
Workflow: .github/workflows/test-on-demand.yml

This workflow runs the Postman test collection against the deployed service with Newman. It takes a tag input (default main) that selects which version of the test collection to run. See Quality Assurance for details.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
Workflow: .github/workflows/deploy-docs-on-demand.yml (in the documentation repository)

This documentation site is built and published by this workflow.

  • Trigger: Manual, with a version number (e.g. 1.0.0) as input.
  • Process:
    1. Installs mkdocs, mkdocs-material, mike, and the other required plugins.
    2. Builds the static site from the Markdown files in docs/.
    3. Uses mike to commit the built site to the gh-pages branch, under the given version.
    4. Points the latest alias at this version and makes latest the default, so visitors see the most recent documentation.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: The Cross-Dataset Discovery service is configured through environment variables. In Kubernetes they are provided by a ConfigMap, a Secret, and the Deployment manifest (see Deployment). The values used in each environment are kept in the deployment repository.

docs.title: Local Development (.env)
docs.text:
For local development, the variables can be placed in a .env file instead. Put it in the cross_dataset_discovery/ directory (the one containing the darelabdb package) and start the service from there:

cd cross_dataset_discovery
uvicorn darelabdb.api_datagems_cross_dataset_discovery.app.main:app --port 8000

Environment variables that are set take precedence over values in .env.

docs.title: Example .env file
docs.text:
# Authentication & authorization
OIDC_ISSUER_URL="https://<identity-provider>/oauth/realms/<realm>"
OIDC_AUDIENCE="cross-dataset-discovery-api"
GATEWAY_API_URL="https://<gateway-host>/gw"

# Search infrastructure
QDRANT_URL="http://localhost:6333"
QDRANT_COLLECTION="cross_dataset_unified"
TEI_URL="http://localhost:8080"

# Ingestion from SQL datasets (only needed to ingest sql-db files)
SQL_DB_BASE_URLS="postgresql://user:password@localhost:5432"

# LLM for /corpus-analysis-search/
LLM_PROVIDER="scayle,bedrock"
SCAYLE_TOKEN="your-scayle-token"
AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK="your-bedrock-api-key"

docs.title: Environment Variables
docs.text: The Default column is the value used when the variable is not set.

docs.title: Authentication & Authorization
docs.text: Variable Description Default OIDC_ISSUER_URL Base URL of the OIDC identity provider. Tokens must be issued by it, and its public keys are used to verify them. https://datagems-dev.scayle.es/oauth/realms/dev OIDC_AUDIENCE The audience (aud) tokens must be issued for. cross-dataset-discovery-api GATEWAY_API_URL Base URL of the DataGEMS Gateway, queried for the caller's dataset grants. https://datagems-dev.scayle.es/gw

docs.title: Search Infrastructure
docs.text: Variable Description Default QDRANT_URL URL of the Qdrant vector database. http://localhost:6333 QDRANT_COLLECTION Qdrant collection holding the indexed datasets. cross_dataset_unified TEI_URL URL of the Text Embeddings Inference (TEI) service that produces dense embeddings. http://localhost:8080 TEI_TIMEOUT Timeout, in seconds, for embedding requests to TEI (during both search and ingestion). 30

docs.title: Ingestion
docs.text: Variable Description Default INGESTION_BATCH_SIZE Number of items embedded and written to Qdrant per batch. Lower values reduce memory use. 64 INGESTION_JOBS_COLLECTION Qdrant collection that stores ingestion job records. Created automatically. <QDRANT_COLLECTION>_ingestion_jobs SQL_DB_BASE_URLS Comma-separated SQLAlchemy URLs of the database servers that host sql-db datasets, without a database name (e.g. postgresql://user:pass@host:5432). For each sql-db file, the servers are tried in order until one has a database with the file's name. If empty, sql-db files are skipped. empty SQL_DB_BASE_URL Single-URL form of SQL_DB_BASE_URLS, kept for compatibility. Used only if SQL_DB_BASE_URLS is empty. empty SQL_DB_MAX_TABLE_MB Tables larger than this (in MB) are not indexed row by row. Instead, each column is indexed once, with the distinct values found in a sample of rows. 0 disables the limit. 512 SQL_DB_SAMPLE_ROWS Number of rows sampled from tables over SQL_DB_MAX_TABLE_MB. 10000 SQL_DB_READ_CHUNK_ROWS Number of rows read from the database at a time when indexing a table row by row. 20000

docs.title: LLM (Corpus Analysis Search)
docs.text:
POST /corpus-analysis-search/ uses an LLM, which can come from two providers:

  • scayle: an OpenAI-compatible endpoint hosted by SCAYLE;
  • bedrock: Amazon Bedrock.

LLM_PROVIDER lists the providers in order of preference. Each LLM call goes to the first provider; if that call fails, the next provider is tried, and so on. If all providers fail, the endpoint falls back to a plain search (see API Overview). | Variable | Description | Default | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | LLM_PROVIDER | Comma-separated list of LLM providers (scayle, bedrock), in order of preference. | scayle,bedrock | | SCAYLE_BASE_URL | Base URL of the SCAYLE LLM service. | https://chat.scayle.es | | SCAYLE_TOKEN | API token for the SCAYLE LLM service, used by the scayle provider. | not set | | SCAYLE_MODEL | Model to use on SCAYLE. | qwen3.8-flash-next | | SCAYLE_VERIFY_TLS | Whether to verify the SCAYLE service's TLS certificate (true / false). | false | | SCAYLE_TIMEOUT | Timeout, in seconds, for SCAYLE requests. | 120 | | SCAYLE_CONNECT_TIMEOUT | Timeout, in seconds, for connecting to SCAYLE. Kept short so an unreachable SCAYLE service quickly falls back to the next provider. | 5 | | BEDROCK_MODEL | Model ID to use on Amazon Bedrock. | eu.anthropic.claude-haiku-5-5 | | AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK | Amazon Bedrock API key. Without it, Bedrock calls fail. | not set |

docs.title: Runtime
docs.text:
Variable Description Default ROOT_PATH Path prefix under which the API is served behind the reverse proxy. Used to build correct links in /swagger and /redoc. empty CHUNK_TOKENIZER_PATH Path to the BAAI/bge-m3 tokenizer.json used for token-based chunking during ingestion. If not set, the tokenizer is downloaded from Hugging Face. The Docker image includes the file and sets this variable. not set FASTEMBED_CACHE_PATH Directory with the cached FastEmbed Qdrant/bm25 model used for sparse (BM25) vectors. The Docker image includes the model and sets this variable. FastEmbed default

DEV_MODE also exists in the settings, but it has no effect on the API. In particular, it does not disable authentication.

docs.title: Fixed Settings
docs.text:
These are set in the code and cannot be changed through configuration:

Setting Value Dense embedding model Whatever model the TEI service serves. It must be BAAI/bge-m3 (1024 dimensions) to match the indexed collection. Sparse embedding model FastEmbed Qdrant/bm25, computed inside the API. Vector quantization Binary quantization, kept in RAM. LLM Temperature 0. Amazon Bedrock is used in region eu-central-1. When a later provider is configured as fallback, SCAYLE requests are not retried, so the fallback takes over at once; otherwise they are retried twice. LLM relevance threshold Results scored below 3 are dropped by POST /corpus-analysis-search/.

docs.title: Secrets
docs.text:
These values are confidential. In Kubernetes they are kept in a secret store and provided to the service through a Secret, never in the ConfigMap:

Variable Used for SCAYLE_TOKEN SCAYLE LLM service token. AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK Amazon Bedrock API key (LLM). SQL_DB_BASE_URLS Contains the database credentials. In Kubernetes it is assembled in the Deployment from separate secret values for the user, password, host and port.

Never commit real secrets to a .env file.

docs.title: Datastores
docs.text: The Cross-Dataset Discovery service stores all of its data in a Qdrant vector database.

docs.title: Vector Database (Qdrant)
docs.text:
• Technology: Qdrant.
  • Location: A shared Qdrant instance in the Kubernetes cluster, configured with QDRANT_URL. Data is persisted by Qdrant on its own volume.
  • Collections: The service uses two collections, both created automatically:
    • the index collection (QDRANT_COLLECTION), holding the searchable content;
    • the ingestion jobs collection (INGESTION_JOBS_COLLECTION, by default <QDRANT_COLLECTION>_ingestion_jobs), holding the job records.

docs.title: Index Collection
docs.text:
Each indexed item (a table row, a document chunk, a dataset description, …) is stored as one point with two named vectors:

Vector Type Details dense Dense, 1024 dimensions Produced by BAAI/bge-m3 via TEI. Cosine distance. Stored on disk, with a binary-quantized copy kept in RAM for fast search. Results are rescored with the full vectors. sparse Sparse (BM25) Term frequencies computed by FastEmbed (Qdrant/bm25). Qdrant applies IDF weighting at query time. The inverted index is stored on disk.

Hybrid search runs a dense and a sparse search and combines the two rankings with Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF).

docs.title: Point Payload
docs.text:
Every point's payload contains these fields, set by the service:

Field Description content The indexed text, returned as content in search results. dataset_id The dataset the item belongs to. Used to filter searches and to find, count and delete a dataset's points. file_object_id The file the item comes from (absent for dataset-level items such as the description). Returned as object_id in search results. original_filename Path of the source file in the dataset storage.

Depending on the file format, the payload also contains:

File format Additional fields csv, xlsx, xls table_id; for Excel files also sheet_name. sql-db database, table_name, table_id; for tables indexed from a sample, also sampled_rows. json All fields of the source record except the indexed text field(s), plus content_field (the name of the field the text came from). See below. docx table_index for items that come from a table in the document. pptx slide_index. ipynb cell_type.

JSON records keep their own fields. For JSON files, every field of the record other than the indexed text is stored in the payload as it is, including nested objects and lists. This keeps any extra information the dataset provides (titles, dates, languages, keywords, …) available alongside the text. If a record field has the same name as one of the service's fields (dataset_id, file_object_id, original_filename), the service's value is kept.

For example, an entry from a JSON encyclopedia dataset, whose record has the fields id, title, text, year, language, metadata, and so on, is stored as (content shortened):

{
  "content": "CURB , in the manege, a chain of iron made fast to the upper part of the branches of the bridle, …",
  "content_field": "text",
  "dataset_id": "<dataset-uuid>",
  "file_object_id": "<file-object-uuid>",
  "original_filename": "/s3/dataset/<dataset-uuid>/data.json",
  "id": "kp-eb0707-055005-4422-v2.xml",
  "dataset": "19th century knowledge project",
  "file_name": "kp-eb0707-055005-4422-v2.xml",
  "title": "CURB",
  "year": "1830-1842",
  "language": "en",
  "metadata": {
    "edition": "Britannica 7th Edition",
    "original_filename": "language/kp-editions/eb07/XML_v2/c7/kp-eb0707-055005-4422-v2.xml",
    "keywords": ["Curbs", "Chains", "Eye", "Rings"],
    "raw_title_string": "CURB"
  }
}

Here content comes from the record's text field, content_field, dataset_id, file_object_id and the top-level original_filename are added by the service, and all other fields are copied from the record. The record's own nested metadata object, including its own original_filename, is kept unchanged.

Only content is embedded; the other fields are metadata. POST /corpus-analysis-search/ returns them as metadata in its results.

During an ingestion, Qdrant's vector index building (HNSW) is paused for the collection, so the upload is fast. It is resumed when the upload finishes, and the quantization is then re-applied.

docs.title: Ingestion Jobs Collection
docs.text: Each ingestion job is stored as one point with no vectors. Its payload is the job record returned by GET /ingest/{job_id}. The collection has payload indexes on status, dataset_id and started_at, used to filter and sort GET /ingest/.

docs.title: Other Data Sources
docs.text:
The service also reads, but never writes, these sources during ingestion:

  • Dataset storage: a volume mounted into the API pod that holds the dataset profiles and the files they reference.
  • Dataset database servers: PostgreSQL servers holding the sql-db datasets, configured with SQL_DB_BASE_URLS.

docs.title: Deployment
docs.text: The Cross-Dataset Discovery service is deployed as a container on Kubernetes, alongside an embedding service (TEI) and a Qdrant vector database.

docs.title: Components
docs.text:
Component What it is Notes API This service: a FastAPI app served by gunicorn with one uvicorn worker, from the ghcr.io/datagems-eosc/cross-dataset-discovery-api image. Runs as a single replica (see Scaling). TEI Hugging Face Text Embeddings Inference serving BAAI/bge-m3. Produces the dense embeddings for search and ingestion. Can run on CPU (text-embeddings-inference:cpu-* image) or on GPU (cuda-* image). Qdrant The vector database holding the index and the ingestion job records. A shared Qdrant instance, not deployed with this service. The collections are created automatically on first ingestion.

The API also depends on these external services:

  • OIDC provider (Keycloak), to validate tokens.
  • DataGEMS Gateway, to look up dataset grants.
  • Dataset database servers (PostgreSQL), to read sql-db datasets during ingestion.
  • LLM providers (SCAYLE and/or Amazon Bedrock), for the LLM steps of POST /corpus-analysis-search/ (see Configuration).

docs.title: Docker Image
docs.text: The image is built from the Dockerfile in the root of the code repository.

docs.title: Build Stages
docs.text:
1. Builder stage (python:3.12-slim):

    • Installs a CPU-only build of PyTorch first, then the API's Python dependencies (requirements.txt). The API runs on CPU, and the default CUDA build of PyTorch would add several GB to the image.
    • Pre-downloads the FastEmbed Qdrant/bm25 model, used to compute sparse (BM25) vectors.
    • Pre-downloads the BAAI/bge-m3 tokenizer, used for token-based chunking during ingestion.

    Because both models are part of the image, the service does not need Hugging Face access at runtime.

  2. Final stage (python:3.12-slim):

    • Copies the installed packages, the model cache and the application code.
    • Sets FASTEMBED_CACHE_PATH and CHUNK_TOKENIZER_PATH to the bundled models.
    • Runs as a non-root user (appuser).
    • Exposes port 8000, with a Docker HEALTHCHECK on /health every 30 seconds.
    • Starts gunicorn with a single uvicorn worker.

docs.title: Build and Run Locally
docs.text:
# 1. Build the image
docker build -t cross-dataset-discovery .

# 2. Run the container (requires network access to Qdrant and TEI)
docker run -p 8000:8000 \
  -e OIDC_ISSUER_URL="https://<identity-provider>/oauth/realms/<realm>" \
  -e GATEWAY_API_URL="https://<gateway-host>/gw" \
  -e QDRANT_URL="http://host.docker.internal:6333" \
  -e QDRANT_COLLECTION="<collection>" \
  -e TEI_URL="http://host.docker.internal:8080" \
  --name cdd-service \
  cross-dataset-discovery

See Configuration for all variables. Mount the storage holding the dataset profiles and files if you want to test ingestion.

docs.title: Publishing
docs.text: Pushing a Git tag that matches v* (e.g. v1.17.2) builds the image and publishes it to ghcr.io/datagems-eosc/cross-dataset-discovery-api under that tag. See Automations.

docs.title: Kubernetes Setup
docs.text:
The manifests are kept in a deployment repository, one per environment (development and production). For the API they define:

  • ConfigMap: the non-secret configuration (OIDC, Gateway, Qdrant, TEI, ingestion settings).
  • Secret: synced from the secret store. Holds the LLM provider tokens and the database credentials (see Configuration).
  • Deployment:
    • The image tag to run.
    • The environment variables, taken from the ConfigMap and the Secret. ROOT_PATH is set to the path prefix the API is served under.
    • A volume with the dataset storage. Dataset profiles and the files they reference are read from it, so path_to_profile and the profiles' source_file paths must point inside this mount.
    • The gunicorn command, overridden to use a longer worker --timeout.
    • The probes: liveness on GET /, readiness on GET /health.
    • Resource requests and limits. Ingestion is the most memory-hungry operation; if the pod runs out of memory during ingestion, lower INGESTION_BATCH_SIZE.
  • Service: exposes port 8000 inside the cluster.
  • Routing: how requests reach the Service depends on the platform setup of each environment. If the API is served under a path prefix, ROOT_PATH must match it.

TEI has its own Deployment, Service and persistent volume (for the model cache), with separate CPU and GPU variants.

docs.title: Scaling
docs.text:
Run the API with one replica and one worker:

  • Ingestion jobs run as background tasks inside the worker that received the request.
  • When the service starts, it marks every unfinished job as interrupted, assuming that no other worker could still be running it.

More replicas or workers would break that assumption.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Access to the code repository and to the deployment repository of the target environment.
  • kubectl configured for the target cluster (including any required VPN).

Verify access by listing the pods in the service's namespace:

kubectl get pods -n <namespace>

You should see a cross-dataset-discovery-api-... pod.

docs.title: 1. Tag a Release
docs.text:
Commit your changes to the code repository, then create and push a version tag:

git tag vX.Y.Z
git push origin vX.Y.Z

docs.title: 2. Wait for the Image Build
docs.text: Follow the build in the code repository's Actions tab. When it finishes, the image ghcr.io/datagems-eosc/cross-dataset-discovery-api:vX.Y.Z is available.

docs.title: 3. Update the Deployment
docs.text:
In the deployment repository, set the new tag in the API Deployment manifest:

image: ghcr.io/datagems-eosc/cross-dataset-discovery-api:vX.Y.Z

If the release needs new or changed settings, update the ConfigMap (or the secret store) as well. Commit the change.

docs.title: 4. Apply
docs.text: Run the deployment repository's on-demand deploy workflow (Deploy to Dev or Deploy to Prod) from its Actions tab, entering the image tag. Make sure the tag is also committed in the manifest (step 3), so the repository matches what is running.

docs.title: 5. Monitor the Rollout
docs.text:
kubectl get pods -n <namespace> -w

The new pod becomes ready once GET /health succeeds; the old pod is then terminated.

When it starts, the new pod marks any unfinished ingestion jobs as interrupted. Avoid deploying while an ingestion is running, or re-run it afterwards with replace=true (see Maintenance).

docs.title: Status & Error Codes
docs.text: The API uses standard HTTP status codes to indicate the success or failure of a request.

docs.title: Status Codes
docs.text:
Status Code Meaning When it is returned 200 OK Success The request was successful. For POST /ingest/, the dataset is already indexed and was skipped (replace=false). 202 Accepted Job scheduled POST /ingest/ scheduled an ingestion job. Poll it with GET /ingest/{job_id}. 400 Bad Request Validation error The request body or parameters are invalid: for example k is out of range, dataset_ids is an empty list, search_mode is unknown, or a required field is missing. For POST /ingest/, the profile could not be read or has no @id. 401 Unauthorized Authentication error The request has no token, or the token is expired, malformed or has an invalid signature. Also returned when the OIDC provider cannot be reached to validate the token. 403 Forbidden Authorization error The token lacks the required role (user, dg_user or a privileged role), or the caller lacks the dataset grant the endpoint needs (dg_ds-edit or dg_ds-delete). See Security. 404 Not Found Not found GET /ingest/{job_id}: no job with this id. DELETE /dataset/{dataset_id}: the dataset is not in the index. Also returned for unknown paths. 405 Method Not Allowed Wrong method The path exists, but not with this HTTP method. 424 Failed Dependency Dependency error A component the request depends on is unavailable. See Failed Dependency Errors. 500 Internal Server Error Unexpected error An unexpected error occurred while processing the request. This includes Qdrant or the embedding service (TEI) failing during a search, ingestion request or deletion, and a malformed analytical pattern sent to POST /search-ap/.

Search requests never fail because of missing dataset permissions. Results the caller may not see are filtered out, so the response may simply contain fewer (or no) results.

docs.title: General Errors
docs.text:
401, 403, 404, 500, and the 400 errors of POST /ingest/ return:

{
  "code": 403,
  "error": "User does not have permission to ingest this dataset."
}
  • code: The HTTP status code.
  • error: A human-readable description of the error.

docs.title: Validation Errors
docs.text:
400 errors caused by an invalid request body or invalid parameters return:

{
  "code": 102,
  "error": "Validation Error",
  "message": [
    {
      "Key": "body.k",
      "Value": ["Input should be greater than 0"]
    }
  ]
}
  • code: Always 102.
  • message: One entry per invalid field. Key is the field's location (e.g. body.dataset_ids, query.path_to_profile) and Value lists the problems found.

docs.title: Failed Dependency Errors
docs.text:
424 errors return:

{
  "code": 104,
  "error": "error communicating with underpinning service",
  "message": {
    "statusCode": 503,
    "source": "Qdrant"
  }
}
  • code: Always 104.
  • message.source: The failing component:
    • SearchComponent: the search component failed to initialize when the service started.
    • Qdrant: the vector database is unreachable (reported by GET /health).
    • TEI: the embedding service is unreachable (reported by GET /health).
    • IngestionJobStore: ingestion jobs could not be saved or read.
  • message.statusCode: The status of the failing component (503 when it is unavailable).
  • message.correlationId, message.payload: Additional details, when available.

docs.title: Other Errors
docs.text:
• Unknown paths (404) and wrong methods (405) return FastAPI's default body, e.g. {"detail": "Not Found"}.
  • A malformed analytical pattern sent to POST /search-ap/, or a Qdrant failure while POST /ingest/ checks whether the dataset is already indexed, returns a plain-text Internal Server Error.

docs.title: Logging & Accounting
docs.text: The service uses structlog to write structured, JSON-formatted logs to standard output, one JSON object per line, following the DataGEMS json-cf-2 log format.

docs.title: Log Structure
docs.text:
Every log entry written by the service contains:

  • Timestamp: ISO 8601 timestamp (UTC).
  • Message: The log message (event), e.g. http_request_finished.
  • LogLevel: The log level.
  • DGCorrelationId: The correlation ID of the HTTP request being processed (see below).
  • SourceContext: The name of the logger that produced the entry, e.g. darelabdb.api_datagems_cross_dataset_discovery.app.main, or accounting for accounting entries.
  • Application: Always cross-dataset-discovery-api.

Additional key-value pairs give context for specific events, for example UserId, dataset_id, job_id, or error.

Example:

{"query": "renewable energy", "k": 5, "mode": "hybrid", "UserId": "3f2c…", "Application": "cross-dataset-discovery-api", "SourceContext": "darelabdb.api_datagems_cross_dataset_discovery.app.main", "Timestamp": "2026-10-29T10:15:02.123456Z", "Message": "Search completed and filtered.", "LogLevel": "Info", "DGCorrelationId": "b060c227-7002-4be8-8b3c-f7f5ecae85a0", "authorized_results_count": 5}

docs.title: Correlation ID
docs.text:
Every HTTP request is assigned a correlation ID:

  • If the incoming request includes an x-tracking-correlation header, its value is used.
  • Otherwise, a new UUID is generated.

The ID is added as DGCorrelationId to the log entries written while the request is processed. It is also returned to the caller in the x-tracking-correlation response header. This makes it possible to trace a request through the service and across DataGEMS services.

docs.title: Request Logging
docs.text:
A middleware logs the end of every HTTP request, except the health checks (GET / and GET /health). The entry has the message http_request_finished and contains:

  • RequestMethod: e.g. GET, POST.
  • RequestPath: The full request URL, including the query string.
  • StatusCode: The response status code.
  • ProcessTimeMS: Processing time in milliseconds.
  • ResponseSize: The response size in bytes.

The level is error for 5xx responses, warning for 4xx, and info otherwise. If the request fails with an unhandled exception, an http_request_unhandled_exception entry with the exception is logged instead.

docs.title: Accounting
docs.text:
Billable user actions are logged as accounting entries, with SourceContext set to accounting. Every accounting entry includes UserId (the token's sub claim), Action, Resource (always CrossDatasetDiscovery) and Timestamp.

Action Logged when Additional fields Search A POST /search/ or POST /search-ap/ request passes the role check. Type (+), Value (1), Measure (Unit) Corpus Search A POST /corpus-analysis-search/ request passes the role check. Type (+), Value (1), Measure (Unit) IngestDataset POST /ingest/ schedules an ingestion job (not when it is skipped). DatasetId, Replace, and ClientId when the token has a clientid claim DeleteDataset DELETE /dataset/{dataset_id} deletes a dataset. DatasetId, DeletedCount, and ClientId when the token has a clientid claim

Example:

{"UserId": "3f2c…", "Action": "Search", "Resource": "CrossDatasetDiscovery", "Type": "+", "Value": 1, "Measure": "Unit", "Timestamp": "2026-10-29T10:15:02.120001Z", "Application": "cross-dataset-discovery-api", "SourceContext": "accounting", "Message": "Search action performed", "LogLevel": "Info", "DGCorrelationId": "b060c227-7002-4be8-8b3c-f7f5ecae85a0"}

docs.title: Maintenance
docs.text:
This page describes routine maintenance tasks: keeping the search index in sync with the datasets, following ingestion jobs, and recovering from failures.

The examples use curl, with the API's base URL in $CDD and a valid access token in $TOKEN:

CDD="https://<host>/cross-dataset-discovery"
TOKEN="<access token>"

Ingesting and deleting a dataset require the corresponding grant on that dataset (dg_ds-edit or dg_ds-delete), or a privileged role (dg_admin, dg_system, dg_dataset-curator). Maintenance across many datasets is easiest with a privileged service account. See Security.

docs.title: Checking Service Health
docs.text:
curl "$CDD/health"

A 200 response means the service is up and can reach Qdrant and the embedding service (TEI). A 424 response names the failing component in message.source. See Status & Error Codes.

docs.title: Adding a Dataset to the Index
docs.text:
Ingest the dataset from its profile:

curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  "$CDD/ingest/?path_to_profile=/s3/path/to/profile.json"

The response contains a job_id. Ingestion runs in the background and can take from seconds to tens of minutes, depending on the dataset size. See Following Ingestion Jobs.

docs.title: Updating a Dataset
docs.text:
If a dataset is already indexed, POST /ingest/ does nothing and returns "status": "skipped". To bring the index up to date after a dataset has changed, re-ingest it with replace=true:

curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  "$CDD/ingest/?path_to_profile=/s3/path/to/profile.json&replace=true"

This deletes all of the dataset's indexed content and rebuilds it from the profile. While the job runs, searches return incomplete results for that dataset.

docs.title: Removing a Dataset from the Index
docs.text:
curl -X DELETE -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "$CDD/dataset/<dataset_id>"

This removes the dataset's indexed content only; the dataset itself is not touched. A 404 response means the dataset was not in the index.

docs.title: Following Ingestion Jobs
docs.text:
Get the status of a job:

curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "$CDD/ingest/<job_id>"

The status moves from pending to running, and ends as completed or failed (or as interrupted, see below).

When a job is completed, compare the counts:

  • items_submitted and items_indexed should be equal. A lower items_indexed means some items could not be embedded or stored and were skipped.
  • After a new ingestion, or one with replace=true, points_in_qdrant should equal items_indexed. A difference means points were lost, or another job wrote to the same dataset at the same time.

List recent jobs, optionally filtered by status or dataset:

# Failed jobs (listing across datasets requires a privileged role)
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "$CDD/ingest/?status=failed&limit=50"

# All jobs of one dataset
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "$CDD/ingest/?dataset_id=<dataset_id>"

docs.title: Recovering from Failed or Interrupted Jobs
docs.text:
• failed: The job stopped with an error, given in the job's error field. Fix the cause, for example a missing file or an unreachable database, then re-ingest the dataset with replace=true.
  • interrupted: The service restarted, for example during a deployment or after a crash, before the job finished. The dataset may be partially indexed. Re-ingest it with replace=true.

In both cases, replace=true is needed to remove any content the failed job had already indexed.

After a deployment or restart, check for interrupted jobs:

curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "$CDD/ingest/?status=interrupted"

To avoid interrupted jobs, do not deploy while an ingestion is running (see Deployment).

docs.title: Rebuilding the Whole Index
docs.text:
There is no endpoint that re-indexes every dataset at once. To rebuild the index, re-ingest every dataset with replace=true (see Updating a Dataset). Each re-ingestion deletes the dataset's existing points and replaces them, so the index is rebuilt in place, in the same collection, without needing space for a second copy. Wait for each job to finish before starting the next, since ingestion is memory-intensive.

A full rebuild is needed when the content already in the index no longer matches what the service would produce now. For example:

  • After a change in how files are processed, such as a new loader or a different chunking.

  • After a change of the embedding model served by TEI. To change the model:

    1. Deploy TEI with the new model.
    2. Re-ingest every dataset with replace=true.

    Until every dataset has been re-ingested, the collection holds vectors from both models. Queries are embedded with the new model, so dense and hybrid search results for datasets that have not been re-ingested yet are unreliable. Sparse (BM25) search is not affected.

The new model must produce 1024-dimensional vectors, like BAAI/bge-m3: the vector size is fixed when the collection is created, and the code expects 1024. A model with a different dimension requires a code change, and the collection must be deleted and rebuilt from scratch.

docs.title: Ingestion Job Records
docs.text: Job records are kept in the ingestion jobs collection in Qdrant (see Datastores). They are never deleted automatically. If the collection grows too large, old records can be deleted directly in Qdrant.

docs.text:
Welcome to the developer guide for the nlp_retrieval framework.

This document provides an overview of the framework's architecture and a step-by-step guide for extending it with new components (like loaders, retrievers, or rerankers) and benchmarking their performance.

docs.title: 1. Framework Overview
docs.text: The nlp_retrieval module provides a modular, configurable, and extensible framework for building and benchmarking end-to-end text retrieval pipelines. It is designed around a "composition over inheritance" model, where a central Searcher orchestrates various independent components to perform indexing and searching tasks.

docs.title: Core Principles
docs.text:
The framework is built on a few key principles:

  • Modularity: Each component is a self-contained, swappable Python class.
  • Clear Interfaces: Components inherit from an Abstract Base Class (ABC) that defines a strict contract for its methods.
  • Standardized Data Flow: We use Pydantic models (SearchableItem, RetrievalResult) to pass data between components.
  • Batch-First Design: All components are designed to operate on batches (List) of queries or results, enabling efficient processing.

docs.title: How the Service Uses the Framework
docs.text:
The Cross-Dataset Discovery API is built on this framework. It uses a Searcher with a single retriever, QdrantHybridRetriever (sparse, dense and hybrid search in Qdrant), and no query processor or reranker. For ingestion it uses the file-format loaders (CsvLoader, XlsxLoader, JsonLoader, DocxLoader, PptxLoader, IpynbLoader, SqlDbLoader, ChunkedContentLoader). See Architecture.

The other components (FAISS, Pyserini/BM25, ColBERT, the rerankers, query processors, and the table retrieval methods) are used for research and benchmarking.

docs.title: Directory Structure
docs.text:
All retrieval-related code resides in cross_dataset_discovery/darelabdb/nlp_retrieval/.

nlp_retrieval/
├── core/                      # Pydantic models
├── loaders/                   # Reads data from sources
├── user_query_processors/     # Processes raw user queries
├── retrievers/                # Indexes data and retrieves candidates
├── rerankers/                 # Re-scores and ranks candidates
├── evaluation/                # Tools for calculating metrics
├── benchmarking/              # Orchestrator for running benchmarks
├── table_retrieval_scripts/   # Unified indexing/benchmark scripts for table retrieval
├── docs/                      # Framework documentation
└── searcher.py                # The main pipeline orchestrator

Each component type has its ABC in its own folder (loaders/loader_abc.py, retrievers/retriever_abc.py, rerankers/reranker_abc.py, user_query_processors/query_processor_abc.py).

docs.title: Core Data Models
docs.text:
Before you start, familiarize yourself with the two fundamental data models defined in darelabdb/nlp_retrieval/core/models.py:

  • SearchableItem: The canonical representation of a single piece of data to be indexed.
  • item_id: str: A unique identifier for the item.
  • content: str: The main text content used for retrieval.
  • metadata: Dict: A dictionary for any associated metadata.
  • RetrievalResult: Represents a single item returned by a search.
  • item: SearchableItem: The retrieved item.
  • score: float: The relevance score assigned by the retriever or reranker.

docs.title: 2. System Architecture & Workflows
docs.text: The framework is built upon a set of abstract base classes (ABCs), each defining a specific role in the retrieval pipeline. The Searcher and Benchmarker classes orchestrate the interaction between these components.

docs.title: Core Components & Interfaces
docs.text:
• BaseLoader: Loads data from a source (e.g., file, database) and converts it into SearchableItems.
  • BaseUserQueryProcessor: Transforms a batch of user queries into a format suitable for retrieval (e.g., decomposition, keyword extraction).
  • BaseRetriever: Manages the indexing of SearchableItems and the retrieval of candidate results.
  • BaseReranker: Re-scores a list of candidate RetrievalResults to improve ranking quality.

docs.title: Available Components
docs.text: Type Classes Loaders (files) CsvLoader, XlsxLoader, JsonLoader, DocumentJsonLoader, DocxLoader, PptxLoader, IpynbLoader, ChunkedContentLoader, DataframesLoader, TableJsonLoader Loaders (databases) SqlDbLoader (SQLAlchemy URL) Loaders (table retrieval methods) AutoDDGLoader, BirdieLoader, JarTableLoader, PneumaLoader, QGpTLoader, TableRAGLoader Retrievers QdrantHybridRetriever, FaissRetriever (dense), PyseriniRetriever (BM25), ColBERTRetriever, RagatouilleColbertRetriever, MinHashLshRetriever, BirdieRetriever, PneumaRetriever, TableRAGRetriever Rerankers MxbaiCrossEncoderReranker, BgeReranker, SentenceTransformerCrossEncoderReranker, BiEncoderReranker, LLMReranker, BridgeReranker, JarMIPReranker, PneumaReranker Query processors PassthroughQueryProcessor (default), DecompositionProcessor, KeywordExtractorProcessor, KeyBERTProcessor, NERQueryProcessor, NgramQueryProcessor, JarDecompositionProcessor, TableRAGQueryProcessor

docs.title: Indexing Workflow
docs.text:
The indexing process is initiated by the Searcher.index(loader, output_path) method.

  1. Load: The loader (e.g., JsonLoader) loads the data into a List[SearchableItem].
  2. Index: The Searcher passes this list to the index() method of each configured retriever (e.g., PyseriniRetriever, FaissRetriever), each with its own subdirectory of output_path, named after the retriever's class.
  3. Store: Each retriever builds its specific index (e.g., a Lucene index, a FAISS vector index) and saves it in that subdirectory.

QdrantHybridRetriever is the exception: it stores everything in Qdrant and ignores output_path.

Figure 1: The indexing workflow showing data flow from source through loader to multiple retrievers creating their respective indexes.

docs.title: Search Workflow
docs.text:
The search process is initiated by the Searcher.search(nlqs, output_path, k, **kwargs) method.

  1. Process Query: The input queries are passed to the configured BaseUserQueryProcessor (PassthroughQueryProcessor if none is set).
  2. Retrieve: The Searcher passes the processed queries to each configured retriever, asking each for k × reranker_multiplier candidates (default multiplier 3). Extra keyword arguments are passed through to the retrievers; QdrantHybridRetriever uses them for search_mode and filters.
  3. Combine (Hybrid Search): The Searcher collects the results from all retrievers into a single pool of candidates, deduplicated by item_id.
  4. Rerank (Optional): If a BaseReranker is configured, this combined pool is passed to its rerank() method for re-scoring.
  5. Return: The final results are returned, sorted by score and truncated to k per query.

Figure 2: The complete search pipeline from query input through processing, retrieval, combination, and optional reranking.

docs.title: General Steps
docs.text:
1. Identify the Component Type: Determine which category your new class falls into: loaders, user_query_processors, retrievers, or rerankers.
  2. Create the File: Add a new Python file in the appropriate directory (e.g., cross_dataset_discovery/darelabdb/nlp_retrieval/retrievers/my_new_retriever.py).
  3. Inherit from the ABC: Your new class must inherit from the correct Abstract Base Class (e.g., BaseRetriever from retriever_abc.py).
  4. Implement All Abstract Methods: Implement every method marked with @abstractmethod in the parent ABC. Make sure your method signatures match the ABC exactly.
  5. Use Core Data Models: Your component must accept and/or return the Pydantic models (SearchableItem, RetrievalResult) as defined in the ABC contract.

docs.title: Creating a New Loader
docs.text:
• Inherit from: BaseLoader
  • Implement:
  • __init__(self, ...): Accept necessary parameters, like file paths or connection details.
  • load(self) -> List[SearchableItem]: Read your data source and create a list of SearchableItem objects.
  • Optionally override:
  • load_stream(self) -> Generator[SearchableItem, None, None]: Yield items one at a time instead of building the whole list. The default implementation calls load(). The service's ingestion uses load_stream(), so override it for any loader that can produce large amounts of data.

docs.title: Creating a New User Query Processor
docs.text:
• Inherit from: BaseUserQueryProcessor
  • Implement:
  • __init__(self, ...): Accept any configuration for your processing logic.
  • process(self, nlqs: List[str]) -> List[List[str]]: Receives a list of raw queries and returns a list of lists, where each inner list contains the processed strings (e.g., sub-queries, keywords) for one input query. The output must have the same length as nlqs.

docs.title: Creating a New Retriever
docs.text:
• Inherit from: BaseRetriever
  • Implement:
  • __init__(self, ...): Initialize your retrieval model, parameters, etc.
  • index(self, items: List[SearchableItem], output_path: str) -> None: Build your search index from the items' content, store whatever is needed to rebuild the SearchableItems at retrieval time, and save all index files inside output_path.
  • retrieve(self, processed_queries_batch: List[List[str]], output_path: str, k: int, **kwargs) -> List[List[RetrievalResult]]: Load the index and process all sub-queries of each original query. Return one aggregated, deduplicated list of RetrievalResult objects per original query (the output must have the same length as processed_queries_batch). Use **kwargs for retriever-specific options.

docs.title: Creating a New Reranker
docs.text:
• Inherit from: BaseReranker
  • Implement:
  • __init__(self, ...): Initialize your reranking model.
  • rerank(self, nlqs: List[str], results_batch: List[List[RetrievalResult]], k: int) -> List[List[RetrievalResult]]: For each query and its candidates, compute new scores, sort the results in descending order, and truncate them to the top k. The output must have the same length as nlqs.

docs.title: Assembling a Pipeline
docs.text:
Once you have created your custom component, you can use it in a Searcher pipeline.

from darelabdb.nlp_retrieval.searcher import Searcher
from darelabdb.nlp_retrieval.loaders.json_loader import JsonLoader
from darelabdb.nlp_retrieval.retrievers.dense_retriever import FaissRetriever
# Import your new custom component
from darelabdb.nlp_retrieval.rerankers.my_reranker import MyReranker

# 1. Initialize the components
my_loader = JsonLoader(
    file_path="path/to/data.jsonl",       # .json (array) or .jsonl
    item_id_prefix="my-dataset:data.jsonl",
    content_fields=["text"],
)
my_retriever = FaissRetriever(model_name_or_path="BAAI/bge-m3")
my_custom_reranker = MyReranker(model_name="some-model")  # Your new reranker

# 2. Assemble the Searcher
searcher = Searcher(
    retrievers=[my_retriever],
    reranker=my_custom_reranker,
)

# 3. Build the index
INDEX_DIR = "./my_index"
searcher.index(loader=my_loader, output_path=INDEX_DIR)

# 4. Search
queries = ["what is the capital of france?", "what is the best gpu for gaming?"]
results = searcher.search(nlqs=queries, output_path=INDEX_DIR, k=5)

print(results)

docs.title: Supporting a New File Format in the Service
docs.text:
To let the API ingest a new file format:

  1. Create a loader for it, as described above, and implement load_stream().
  2. Add a branch for the format's original_format value in _build_items() in darelabdb/api_datagems_cross_dataset_discovery/app/main.py, creating your loader with the file's path and the shared metadata (dataset_id, file_object_id, original_filename).
  3. Document the format in the API Overview.

docs.title: 4. Part 2: Evaluating Your New Component
docs.text:
After creating a new component, the next step is to measure its performance. The framework provides tools to run automated benchmarks and calculate standard information retrieval metrics.

Figure 3: The benchmarking pipeline showing the complete flow from configuration through evaluation and logging.

docs.title: Key Evaluation Classes
docs.text:
• RetrievalEvaluator (darelabdb/nlp_retrieval/evaluation/evaluator.py): The core engine for calculating metrics such as Precision, Recall, F1-Score and Perfect Recall.
  • Benchmarker (darelabdb/nlp_retrieval/benchmarking/benchmarker.py): The high-level orchestrator. It runs different Searcher configurations, calls the RetrievalEvaluator, and logs results to the console and to Weights & Biases.

docs.title: The Matching Logic
docs.text:
This is the most important concept in our evaluation system. A predicted item is considered a "correct hit" if its metadata contains all the key-value pairs of a gold standard item's metadata.

Example:

  • Gold Standard Metadata: {'page_title': 'Mashable', 'source': 'some_sentence'}
  • Prediction 1 Metadata: {'page_title': 'Mashable', 'source': 'some_sentence', 'value': 'xyz'} → MATCH (a superset)
  • Prediction 2 Metadata: {'page_title': 'Mashable', 'source': 'another_sentence'} → NO MATCH

The evaluator also handles granularity automatically. When computing metrics @k, k refers to the number of unique entities, as defined by the gold standard's metadata keys. For example, if the gold standard metadata is {'page_title': 'A'}, the predictions are first deduplicated to keep only the first item for each unique page_title, and the metrics are calculated on that list.

docs.title: How to Run a Benchmark
docs.text: The table retrieval script table_retrieval_scripts/run_benchmark.py is a complete example of setting up and running an evaluation.

docs.title: Step 1: Prepare the Corpus Loader
docs.text:
The Benchmarker does not depend on your data's format. It only needs an initialized loader whose load() method returns a List[SearchableItem].

from darelabdb.nlp_retrieval.loaders.json_loader import JsonLoader

loader = JsonLoader(
    file_path="path/to/corpus.jsonl",
    item_id_prefix="corpus",
    content_fields=["title", "abstract"],      # each field becomes a separate item
    record_id_field="id",
    metadata_fields=["page_title", "source"],  # None = all remaining fields
)

docs.title: Step 2: Prepare Queries and Gold Standard
docs.text:
The Benchmarker does not read a specific benchmark file. You create two lists in memory:

  • queries: List[str]: A list of query strings.
  • gold_standard: List[List[RetrievalResult]]: A parallel list, where each inner list contains the correct RetrievalResult objects for the corresponding query.

For the gold standard, only the metadata of each item is used for matching; item_id and content can be placeholders:

from darelabdb.nlp_retrieval.core.models import RetrievalResult, SearchableItem

gold_item = SearchableItem(
    item_id="placeholder",
    content="placeholder",
    metadata={"page_title": "Mashable", "source": "some_sentence"},
)
gold_standard_for_one_query = [RetrievalResult(item=gold_item, score=1.0)]

docs.title: Step 3: Configure Your Searcher Pipelines
docs.text:
Create an initialized Searcher instance for each configuration you want to test, including your new component.

from darelabdb.nlp_retrieval.retrievers.bm25_retriever import PyseriniRetriever

# Configuration 1: Baseline
bm25_searcher = Searcher(retrievers=[PyseriniRetriever()])

# Configuration 2: Your new component
my_new_searcher = Searcher(retrievers=[MyNewRetriever()])

# Create a list of named configurations for the Benchmarker
searcher_configs = [
    ("BM25_Baseline", bm25_searcher),
    ("My_New_Retriever", my_new_searcher),
]

PyseriniRetriever requires a Java 21 JDK.

docs.title: Step 4: Initialize and Run the Benchmarker
docs.text:
Pass all the prepared objects to the Benchmarker and call .run().

from darelabdb.nlp_retrieval.benchmarking.benchmarker import Benchmarker
from darelabdb.nlp_retrieval.evaluation.evaluator import RetrievalEvaluator

evaluator = RetrievalEvaluator()
benchmarker = Benchmarker(
    searcher_configs=searcher_configs,
    evaluator=evaluator,
    loader=loader,
    queries=queries,
    gold_standard=gold_standard,
    k_values=[1, 5, 10],
    output_path="./benchmark_results",
    use_wandb=True,
    wandb_project="my-retrieval-project",
    wandb_entity="my-username",
)

benchmarker.run()

docs.title: Interpreting the Output
docs.text:
• Console Output: For each configuration, the indexing status, the search speed (queries per second), the metrics for the full retrieved set, and the metrics @k for each value in k_values. At the end, a summary table compares all runs at the largest k.
  • Weights & Biases (W&B) Dashboard: If use_wandb=True, the Benchmarker creates:
    • one run per configuration, with the configuration of all its components, the final metrics, and a performance_metrics_at_k table;
    • a Benchmark_Summary_Report run, with a benchmark_summary_table comparing all configurations.

docs.title: 5. Table Retrieval Benchmarks
docs.text:
The framework includes a suite for evaluating table retrieval methods, documented in detail in nlp_retrieval/docs/TABLE_RETRIEVAL.md.

  • Methods: standard baselines (bm25, dense, colbert) and LLM-augmented or specialized methods (autoddg, birdie, jar, pneuma, qgpt, tablerag).
  • Data: The benchmarks are stored in the DARELab/table_retrieval_data Hugging Face dataset repository. Each benchmark has a corpus.json (the tables) and a queries.json (queries with their gold table_ids). Only the requested benchmarks are downloaded and cached.
  • Scripts: table_retrieval_scripts/run_indexing.py builds the indexes (and caches any LLM-generated augmentations), and table_retrieval_scripts/run_benchmark.py evaluates them. Both take --method <name> or --method all. They load each method's models once and process all benchmarks with it before moving to the next method, so that large LLMs do not exhaust GPU memory.
  • Benchmark registry: The scripts load the benchmarks through the darelabdb.utils_datasets package of the DARELab monorepo (table_retrieval_benchmarks.py), where new benchmarks are registered.
