docs.title: Quality Assurance
docs.text: Quality assurance (QA) combines automated static analysis, vulnerability scanning, and API-level integration testing to ensure the service functions as expected.

docs.title: Code Analysis
docs.text:
We use GitHub CodeQL for static analysis of the source code. This process helps identify potential bugs, security vulnerabilities, and quality issues before they impact production.

  • Technology: GitHub CodeQL
  • Targets: The analysis runs on both the Python source code and the GitHub Actions workflow files themselves.
  • Checks: It uses a set of queries to find common vulnerabilities (e.g., injection flaws, insecure data handling), bugs, and code quality anti-patterns.
  • Execution: The analysis is performed by the on-demand code-scan-on-demand.yml workflow. Results and alerts are available directly in the repository's "Security" tab.

docs.title: Code Metrics
docs.text:
To ensure the long-term maintainability and readability of the code, we use the Radon library to generate code metrics.

  • Technology: Radon
  • Metrics:
    • Maintainability Index (MI): A score from 0-100 indicating how easy the code is to maintain (higher is better).
    • Cyclomatic Complexity (CC): Measures the number of independent paths through the code. A lower score indicates simpler, less complex code.
    • Lines of Code (LOC): Provides raw metrics on the size of the codebase.
  • Execution: The metrics are generated by the on-demand code-metrics-on-demand.yml workflow, which produces a downloadable code-metrics-report.txt artifact.

docs.title: Vulnerability Checks
docs.text:
We use Trivy to scan for known vulnerabilities in our dependencies and container image, ensuring the service is secure from common threats.

  • Technology: Trivy
  • Scans:
    1. Configuration Scan: Scans the Dockerfile and other repository files for security misconfigurations.
    2. Image Scan: Scans the final Docker image for known vulnerabilities (CVEs) with CRITICAL or HIGH severity in its OS packages and Python libraries.
  • Execution: The scan is performed by the on-demand vulnerability-scan-on-demand.yml workflow. It requires an image tag as input and uploads detailed JSON reports as build artifacts.

docs.title: Testing
docs.text:
The service's functionality is validated through API-level integration tests using Postman and its command-line runner, Newman.

  • Test Suite: The test cases are defined in the Postman collection located at tests/cross-dataset-discovery-api-tests.postman_collection.json.

  • Test Cases: The suite includes the following tests:

    • Health Check: Verifies that the /health endpoint is available and returns a 200 OK status, indicating the service and its dependencies are healthy.
    • Get User Access Token: Simulates a user login against the OIDC provider to acquire a valid JWT, which is required for all protected endpoints.
    • Perform Search - Valid Request: Executes a valid search against the /search/ endpoint and asserts that the response is successful (200 OK) and has the correct structure.
    • Perform Search - Bad Request: Sends a request with an invalid payload (an empty dataset_ids list) and asserts that the API correctly rejects it with a 400 Bad Request status.

    If the health check fails, the remaining requests are skipped.

  • Coverage: The suite covers only GET /health and POST /search/. The other endpoints (POST /search-ap/, POST /corpus-analysis-search/, the ingestion endpoints, and DELETE /dataset/{dataset_id}) are not tested automatically. The repository has no unit tests.

docs.title: How to Run Tests
docs.text:
The API tests are designed to be run automatically via a GitHub Actions workflow.

  • Workflow File: .github/workflows/test-on-demand.yml
  • Trigger: The workflow is triggered manually (workflow_dispatch) from the Actions tab in the GitHub repository.
  • Process:
    1. Navigate to the "Actions" tab and select the "Test Scenario (On-Demand)" workflow.
    2. Click "Run workflow". You will be prompted to enter a tag (e.g., main or a specific version like v1.0.0) to test against.
    3. The workflow checks out the specified version of the code, which determines the version of the test collection that is run. The tests are always run against the deployed service, not against a build of that version.
    4. It then uses the official postman/newman Docker image to execute the test collection.
    5. All necessary environment variables (API base URL, credentials, etc.) are securely injected into the test run from the repository's secrets.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
Authentication is handled via the OAuth 2.0 and OpenID Connect (OIDC) protocols. Every request to a protected endpoint must include a valid JSON Web Token (JWT) in the Authorization header as a Bearer token.

The service validates incoming JWTs against the public keys (JWKS) of the OIDC provider configured in OIDC_ISSUER_URL. It verifies:

  • the signature (RS256),
  • the issuer (OIDC_ISSUER_URL),
  • the audience (OIDC_AUDIENCE, cross-dataset-discovery-api by default),
  • the expiry.

If the token is missing, invalid or expired, the API responds with 401 Unauthorized. If the OIDC provider cannot be reached to fetch its keys, the API also responds with 401.

The OIDC configuration and public keys are fetched on the first authenticated request and then cached for the lifetime of the service process.

docs.title: Unauthenticated Endpoints
docs.text:
The following endpoints do not require a token:

  • GET / (liveness check)
  • GET /health (readiness check)
  • GET /swagger, GET /redoc, GET /openapi.json (API documentation)

docs.title: Authorization
docs.text:
Authorization has two layers:

  1. A role check on the token, which applies to every protected endpoint.
  2. A dataset-level check against the DataGEMS Gateway, which depends on the endpoint.

docs.title: Roles
docs.text:
The service reads roles from the token's realm_access.roles claim. To call any protected endpoint, the token must contain at least one of:

  • user
  • dg_user
  • a privileged role (below)

Otherwise the API responds with 403 Forbidden.

docs.title: Privileged Roles
docs.text:
These realm roles grant access to every dataset and skip all dataset-level checks:

  • dg_admin
  • dg_system (for system pipelines, e.g. maintenance tasks run by service accounts)
  • dg_dataset-curator

A caller with one of these roles can search all datasets without filtering, ingest or delete any dataset, and list all ingestion jobs.

docs.title: Dataset-Level Permissions
docs.text:
For callers without a privileged role, the service asks the DataGEMS Gateway which datasets the caller may act on.

It calls the Gateway's POST {GATEWAY_API_URL}/api/principal/context-grants/query endpoint, passing the caller's own token, with a body such as {"roles": ["dg_ds-browse"]}. The grants returned for datasets give the list of dataset IDs the caller holds that grant on.

The grant required depends on the endpoint:

Endpoint Grant required Effect POST /search/, POST /search-ap/, POST /corpus-analysis-search/ dg_ds-browse Results are filtered to the datasets the caller holds this grant on. POST /ingest/ dg_ds-edit on the profile's dataset Otherwise 403. GET /ingest/{job_id} dg_ds-edit on the job's dataset Otherwise 403. GET /ingest/ dg_ds-edit on the dataset_id filter Without a privileged role, dataset_id is required. Otherwise 403. DELETE /dataset/{dataset_id} dg_ds-delete on the dataset Otherwise 403.

docs.title: Search Filtering
docs.text:
• If a search request includes dataset_ids, the service intersects this list with the caller's authorized datasets and searches only the datasets in both lists. If none are left, it returns an empty result list.
  • All search results, regardless of the input filter, are always filtered against the caller's authorized dataset list before being returned. This ensures a caller can never see data from a dataset they are not permitted to access.

docs.title: Gateway Failures
docs.text:
If the Gateway call fails (an error response or a network error), the service treats the caller as having no dataset grants and logs the error. This fails closed:

  • searches return no results;
  • ingestion, job status and deletion requests are rejected with 403.

Callers with a privileged role are not affected, because the Gateway is not called for them.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
The authentication and authorization settings are OIDC_ISSUER_URL, OIDC_AUDIENCE and GATEWAY_API_URL. See Configuration.

The DEV_MODE setting does not disable authentication in the API. It only affects the local Streamlit test app.
